content.title: About
content.content: Turkish coffee is a finely ground coffee brewed in a special pot (cezve) and served in small cups. The preparation involves bringing the mixture to a boil several times, creating a thick foam and a rich aroma. Traditionally it is unfiltered, often sweetened and sometimes flavored with cardamom or other spices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Turkish coffee is one of the oldest coffee preparation methods, with a history of over 500 years.
In Turkey and many Middle Eastern countries coffee is served with a glass of water to cleanse the palate.
The coffee grounds left in the cup are used for fortune‑telling, a practice known as tasseography.
Turkish coffee was inscribed on UNESCO’s Intangible Cultural Heritage list.
Traditional preparation requires slow heating over low heat to avoid over‑boiling.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Coffee contains polyphenols that help combat free radicals and may reduce the risk of chronic diseases.

items.title: Improves alertness
items.content: Caffeine stimulates the central nervous system, enhancing concentration and reaction time.

items.title: Supports metabolism
items.content: Moderate coffee consumption can boost metabolic rate and aid fat oxidation.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Turkish coffee provides magnesium, potassium and manganese, important for muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Enhances mood
items.content: Caffeine promotes the release of dopamine and serotonin, which can improve mood.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: Some individuals may experience anxiety, insomnia or rapid heartbeat after coffee.

items.title: Increased stomach acidity
items.content: Coffee can aggravate gastritis and heartburn in susceptible people.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Caffeine may amplify the effects of certain medications, such as antidepressants and stimulants.

items.title: Potential risk for pregnant women
items.content: Pregnant women are advised to limit caffeine intake to about 200 mg per day.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Prepare Turkish coffee in a cezve by adding cold water, finely ground coffee and sugar to taste. Bring the mixture to a boil 2–3 times, then pour into small cups and let the grounds settle. Serve without milk, optionally flavored with cardamom or cinnamon.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store ground Turkish coffee in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from light. For best flavor use within 2–3 months of grinding. Keep moisture out to prevent clumping.
